feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital communications CV with clear positioning, credible public-sector experience, and good evidence of scope across platforms, governance, analytics, and multimedia. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, tighter structure, and less repetition across skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: progression at NACo is easy to follow and supports the “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader” brand well.  
- Good credibility and scope: Drupal modernization, analytics stack, AI search, video studio buildout, and multi-channel operations show breadth and seniority.  
- Writing quality is strong: concise, polished, and mostly consistent in tone; no obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics beyond activity/scope: e.g., traffic growth, engagement lifts, production savings, search improvements, campaign results, or adoption gains.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap significantly; consolidate to create more space for achievements.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” should lose the comma; punctuation is inconsistent between sections; “French (A2/Learning)” reads awkwardly—use “French (A2, learning)” or “Elementary (A2).” Also consider whether “Coleman DAVIS” should use standard title case for consistency.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning and clear seniority, but the intro is broad and repeats several competency/experience details already covered elsewhere. It would be stronger with one sharper value proposition and more concrete scope.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and reduce list-like phrasing; replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with more direct language.
- Add scale or audience context from recent roles (for example, enterprise public-sector websites, high-volume/member-facing communications, or multi-publisher environments).
- Keep the header aligned with the subtitle by emphasizing digital platforms, governance, and communications systems leadership.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web ecosystems for public-sector and mission-driven organizations. Combines digital strategy, governance, analytics, and editorial operations to improve large-scale content publishing, audience engagement, and cross-channel communications. Brings hands-on leadership across Drupal platforms, multimedia production, and AI-enabled content discovery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Analytics infrastructure,” “editorial systems,” “multimedia production,” and “AI-enabled user experiences” duplicate Core Competencies/Topline Skills.
- “Public-sector communications” is already well established in the experience section; avoid overexplaining it here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It will be more effective if tightened, made more parallel in style, and skewed toward distinctive leadership-level strengths.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, noun-led phrases with consistent structure; avoid mixing systems, functions, and outcomes in one list.
- Replace broader items with sharper terms tied to senior scope and recent work, e.g., “Enterprise web modernization” and “Digital governance and publishing operations.”
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and publishing operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space allows, swap “content experiences” for “content discovery,” which is more specific and less generic.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” overlaps with the header and Recent Projects.
- Several items duplicate Topline Skills almost verbatim, especially governance, analytics, multi-channel communications, and multimedia.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with achievements already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and making the format more parallel will improve scanability and impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and distinguish this from core experience.
- Use parallel, outcome-oriented phrasing: “Launched/Built/Developed…” and trim stacked nouns.
- Clarify technical value in simpler terms, e.g., “hybrid retrieval and vector search” without repeating “AI-enabled” and “AI chat.”
- Standardize style and punctuation; spell out “10 x 20-foot” for consistency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely repeat bullets in the current freelance and NACo roles.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item; consider keeping only 2–3 projects here that add new evidence beyond Work Experience.

items.title: Core Competencies

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Make it sharper by foregrounding scope, platform leadership, and any measurable outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with a stronger lead: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-led bullets; start with verbs like “Led,” “Built,” “Developed,” “Advised,” “Launched.”
- Add scale/results where possible: number of sites/pages/users, campaign launches, workflow time saved, publishing speed, search relevance gains, toolkit downloads, or stakeholder teams supported.
- Tighten phrasing, e.g.: “Built Drupal microsites, modular storytelling components, and member toolkits; improved CMS workflows, front-end delivery, analytics, and cross-channel governance; led AI-enabled search strategy spanning retrieval, structured content, and discovery UX.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects section; keep this bullet high-level here.
- Governance/analytics/workflows also repeat prior NACo roles, so emphasize what is new in this engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if the opening is tighter, bullets start with outcomes, and channel-management language is reduced where older NACo roles already cover execution.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opener with: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget strategy for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable outcomes where missing: growth in email engagement, social reach, production volume, reporting speed, cost savings from the studio, or governance efficiency.
- Tighten phrasing: “Expanded analytics infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, enabling stronger leadership reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on leadership, modernization, infrastructure, and governance.
- Video-program language may duplicate older NACo entries; emphasize building the in-house studio and scaling organizational capacity instead.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what you owned at this level: executional leadership, editorial coordination, and channel growth.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution for advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show ownership and outcome: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is too close to the Director of Digital Media entry.
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager role and footer project.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent experience. It should be tightened to emphasize senior leadership scope and avoid generic phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad nouns with sharper leadership language: “Enterprise digital strategy” → “Enterprise digital strategy and transformation”
- Make the list more distinctive and aligned to recent roles:
- Enterprise digital strategy and transformation
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” to sound more senior and less campaign-copy focused.
- Keep all bullets parallel in structure; avoid mixing systems, leadership, and planning phrased at different levels.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial systems and governance” duplicates “Digital governance & editorial systems” in Core Competencies.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” and “Audience-focused content planning” are already strongly evidenced in recent NACo and consulting roles, so this section should stay concise rather than repeat detail.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it’s too tool-list-heavy and overlaps with the more detailed “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a raw list to grouped, higher-value capabilities: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put the strongest/recent items first: lead with Drupal, CMS modernization, and AI-enabled search; move older/general platforms later or remove from topline.
- Consider dropping one or two lower-priority platforms here: e.g., “WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages” can live in “Technical + IT” unless central to target roles.
- If space allows, sharpen phrasing: replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable workflow systems” or “Airtable-based operational systems.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep topline strategic, not exhaustive.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating identical wording.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. Tighten it to emphasize decision support, measurement, and optimization outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from software-only list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics infrastructure & performance optimization.”
- Use grouped, higher-signal wording: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity.”
- Replace generic items with outcome-oriented terms: “KPI framework design,” “executive/leadership dashboards,” “web performance and SEO analysis.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics infrastructure (GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity) • KPI framework design • Executive reporting dashboards • SEO and web performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep this version concise and strategic, and leave full tool inventory to Technical + IT.
- “Leadership reporting” is weaker than “executive reporting dashboards” and may duplicate broader leadership language elsewhere.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize higher-value production leadership and event delivery rather than generic media tasks.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from task list to capability/ownership language: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “Studio and control-room operations.”
- Remove weaker/generic phrasing like “Video production and editing” and “Livestreaming”; they read junior compared with the seniority shown in recent roles.
- Add one specificity cue tied to recent experience, e.g. “In-house studio buildout and PTZ camera workflows” or “Virtual, hybrid and on-site event production.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • Studio buildout and operations • PTZ camera and multi-camera workflows • Virtual, hybrid and on-site production”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Multimedia production” and “livestream operations” already appear in Core Competencies; use this section to be more specific/technical.
- Tool-level items may also overlap with “Multimedia & Creative Tools,” so avoid repeating software here.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent CMS expertise or expanded with level/context.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize by depth and recency: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint** • **Power Pages** • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, add proficiency cues instead of just names: **Drupal (advanced)** • **WordPress (strong)** • **SharePoint / Power Pages (working knowledge)** • GitHub Pages
- Consider renaming to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner alignment with the rest of the CV.
- If you want more impact, swap GitHub Pages for a more strategic descriptor: **Static site publishing (GitHub Pages)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one list or making this version proficiency-based.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid repeating it elsewhere without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools actually used in recent roles and group items more clearly.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Front-end & implementation:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery; **Integrations & deployment:** API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers unless they matter; “HTML” and “CSS” are cleaner than “HTML5/CSS3.”
- If accurate, replace broad terms with stronger specifics tied to recent work, e.g. “REST API integrations,” “CI/CD with GitHub Actions,” or “serverless scripting with Cloudflare Workers.”
- Consider adding one proof point in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, such as deployment automation, tagging implementation, or custom Drupal front-end work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; avoid expanding this item into that territory.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already highlighted elsewhere. Make it more purposeful by grouping tools by function and emphasizing the platforms most tied to recent systems/governance work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by category, e.g.: **Automation & Workflow Systems:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; **Work Management & Collaboration:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp, Slack, Microsoft Teams
- Put the strongest/recently relevant tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana
- Standardize naming for professionalism: use **Microsoft Teams** instead of Teams
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to impact: “workflow automation, editorial coordination, and cross-team project management”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here
- Slack/Teams may feel generic unless collaboration tools are consistently listed across other technical categories

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare relative to the rest of the CV. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this line should stay tool-focused and avoid restating channel ownership.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform naming for readability and ATS: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers instead of generic tools: **enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- Optional stronger version: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (campaign automation, newsletter distribution, audience segmentation)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding claims like “managed newsletters” or “led email strategy” here; those are already covered in the NACo experience entries.
- If Dynamics 365 was not used in a recent role, consider dropping it or moving it later in the list so the most relevant/current platforms lead.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” In Technical + IT, make it more tool-focused and tighten the wording.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI reporting**
- Swap **SEO** for **Google Search Console** or **technical SEO analysis**; “SEO” is too broad for a tools list.
- Replace **Dashboarding** with **KPI reporting** or **executive dashboards** to sound more outcome-oriented and specific.
- Order by strongest/recently used tools first: GA4, Clarity, BigQuery, Power BI/Looker Studio aligns with your 2022–2024 leadership work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates **Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; keep Technical + IT strictly to platforms/tools, and leave broader capabilities there.
- If A/B testing is not evidenced elsewhere on the CV, consider removing it to avoid an unsupported claim.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational: emphasize team-building, early platform/content operations, and any concrete output or scale.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function…”
- Add scope/results where possible: website refresh size/traffic, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience reach, or workflow improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic verbs: replace “high-impact digital content” with specific deliverables like “livestreamed events, weekly advocacy video updates, and web/social content.”
- Suggested version: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped build NACo’s first in-house digital media team, improving workflows across web, email, social and video. Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreamed events and weekly video updates, while providing day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/building the capability.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; use more junior, execution-focused language here.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch and cross-functional project support, and trim broad phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the differentiator: “Launched NACo’s first podcast…” rather than ending with it.
- Replace vague language like “coordinated innovation and research projects” with clearer scope: program/policy research support, stakeholder coordination, or content development.
- Tighten to one sentence or two concise bullets; example: “Supported innovation and research initiatives for NACo program and policy teams, coordinating project inputs and developing related digital/multimedia content. Launched the organization’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, production, and rollout.”
- If possible, add outcomes: number of episodes, audience growth, internal adoption, or programs supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on podcast launch and innovation/project coordination.
- Avoid overstating leadership here since stronger management achievements appear in 2018–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills, but this item is broad and partly overlaps with stronger multimedia claims elsewhere. Make it more tool-specific and current, emphasizing production capability rather than generic creative software.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Broadcast/livestream studio operations • Podcast recording, editing & production**
